name: Who's Crying Now
reference: Who's Crying Now, outro solo (quarter = 120 BPM, A minor): Journey, Escape (1981, Fantasy Studios, Berkeley, April-June 1981; prod. Kevin Elson and Mike Stone; Neal Schon)
rig: Documented: Schon's black 1977 Gibson Les Paul Pro/Deluxe (originally P-90s, maple neck, ebony board; Schon: 'That's the guitar on a lot of Frontiers, Escape ... and on solos like Who's Crying Now', 'It has a nice, natural compression to it'). Undocumented: the amp, cab and pedals for Escape. The only named amp is Steve Perry's recollection of telling Schon, about this solo, 'I saw you play the Starwood with a Fender Twin ... just plug it in and sketch a little bit'; forum hearsay says Fender Twin with a wah slightly open, or 'a little Roland amp'. Elson: 'Neal always used his own effects', guitars miked with Sony C37, AKG 414 and SM57 (his memory of Open Arms), Neve 8108 / Studer A800, EMT plates and tape delay in the room. Perry: the solo was the simplest take, built from about four drop-in sections, and he refused the label's request to fade it.
notes: APPROXIMATION: the Escape amp is undocumented (no interview, Mix piece or rig rundown names it; only the guitar is on the record). Built on the one amp anybody named for this solo, Perry's Fender Twin: a 1971 Silverface Twin Reverb (period-correct) captured cranked, normal channel V10 T7 M7 B4, into the same Twin's own 2x12 Oxford 12T6-10 speakers on an SM57 at the cap edge (the SM57 is on Elson's list). The cranked Twin plus a humbucker gives the smooth, compressed sustain Schon credits to the guitar; there is no documented compressor, and a NAM capture can't model a compressor's timing, so none is added. SW8 BOOST = TS9 clean push, for more singing sustain on the long held bends (not documented). SW9 DELAY is ON at load: 500 ms (a quarter note at the published 120 BPM), feedback 0.3, cutoff 4500 Hz (Fantasy's tape delay, darker repeats), mix 0.2; 375 ms is the dotted-eighth alternative. 480L Large Plate at 25% stands in for Fantasy's EMT plates. Disputed or missing: a wah 'slightly open' (forum hearsay; SW6 + EXP A parks the DAW wah), the 'little Roland amp' reading, the P-90 vs humbucker question, the double-tracked lead (mono preset). Levelled offline with rigsim --exact to -14 LUFS.

left.label: Ibanez TS9 clean push, D0 T6 L10 (more sustain for the held bends, not documented)
1971 Fender Twin Reverb, cranked, Normal V10 T7 M7 B4 (Perry: 'a Fender Twin'; amp undocumented)
1971 Twin Reverb 2x12 Oxford 12T6-10, SM57 cap edge
Tape delay 500 ms (quarter note at 120 BPM, on)
Lexicon 480L Large Plate (Fantasy Studios EMT plate stand-in)
